name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
coordinate_note: No single published point for the whole region was used.
evidence_note: Parent context only. Upper valleys and lower valleys are separate sites.

name: University Valley
coordinate_note: Geometry is Marinova et al. 2011: 77 deg 51.8 min S, 160 deg 43 min E, Quartermain Mountains, about 1730 m. The same abstract also says about 1700 m. Williams et al. 2018 print 77.868 S, 163.758 E and 1700 m. That longitude is not the Quartermain site next to Beacon Valley.
evidence_note: Dry permafrost over an ice table that deepens from the valley head to the mouth. Phoenix comparison uses this valley against lower Taylor Valley.

name: Central Beacon Valley polygon site
coordinate_note: Geometry is the Liu et al. 2018 thermistor polygon: 77 deg 49 min S, 160 deg 39 min E. Liu et al. 2015 give Beacon Valley as 77 deg 49 min S, 161 deg 39 min E. Elevation 1350 m is the middle-valley floor stated in Liu et al. 2015, not a survey of the thermistor.
evidence_note: Massive ground ice 30-50 cm down, under sublimation till, on one polygon. Not a centroid for the whole valley.

name: Victoria Valley ice-cemented soil
coordinate_note: Hagedorn et al. 2007 give about 450 m elevation and do not print a latitude and longitude for the soil pit.
evidence_note: Lower-elevation ice-cemented soil where summer snow can slow ice loss. Not the University Valley stability regime.

name: Lower Taylor Valley
coordinate_note: The opened Tamppari et al. 2012 abstract does not give a soil-pit coordinate.
evidence_note: In-region contrast to University Valley: summer thaw, aqueous salt transport, and higher biomass.

name: Don Juan Pond
coordinate_note: Dickson et al. 2013 place a time-lapse camera at 77.563 S, 161.256 E on the Dais. That is a vantage point, not the pond, so no geometry is stored. Representative pond coordinate; not the Dickson et al. camera point.
evidence_note: CaCl2 brine in the South Fork of upper Wright Valley, fed by near-surface water tracks and deliquescence rather than observed deep groundwater.

name: Blood Falls
coordinate_note: The opened Mikucki et al. 2009 paper describes the Taylor Glacier outflow and does not print a coordinate used here.
evidence_note: Subglacial ferrous brine. Kept separate from dry permafrost. Not a search seed: the 2009 paper's stated comparison is organic-starved oceans.

name: Askja and Dyngjufjoll
coordinate_note: The parent volcanic system is not given a single point. The caldera summit is a child site.
evidence_note: Context for the basaltic sand sheet. The caldera lake and 1875 pumice are not the Stimson analog.

name: Askja caldera summit
coordinate_note: Wikipedia, citing the Global Volcanism Program: 65.033 N, 16.783 W, summit elevation 1516 m. The same page says the main crater floor is about 1100 m, which is a different surface.
evidence_note: Volcanic context and the 1875 caldera. Not the eolian sand-sheet analog.

name: Dyngjusandur sand sheet
coordinate_note: Sara et al. 2017 place the sheet east-southeast of the caldera, about 40 km long and 240 km2, and do not print a centroid. Approximate location within Dyngjusandur sand-sheet region; not a verified facies centroid.
evidence_note: Basaltic eolian sand sheet used as a Stimson formation analog. Facies are child sites.

name: Dyngjusandur southwest deflationary facies
coordinate_note: Described by Mountney and Russell and by Sara et al. 2017. No corner coordinates were printed in the opened abstract. Approximate sample-location proxy in southwest sand-sheet area; facies assignment requires review.
evidence_note: Deflationary very fine to medium basaltic sand with cobbles and boulders.

name: Dyngjusandur central inflating facies
coordinate_note: No centroid was printed in the opened Sara abstract. Approximate sample-location proxy for central sand-sheet area; facies assignment requires review.
evidence_note: Inflating very fine sand, relict lava, and ripples. This is the main morphological comparison with Stimson cross-bedding.

name: Dyngjusandur northeast pumice-rich facies
coordinate_note: Located only as the northeast portion of the sheet. Approximate northeast sample-area proxy; not verified as pumice-rich facies.
evidence_note: Pumice from the 1875 eruption plus local basalt. Sara et al. set it aside because the chemistry differs.

name: Holuhraun 2014-2015 lava
coordinate_note: Sara et al. 2017 map it on the southeastern sand sheet and do not print a coordinate in the text.
evidence_note: Later lava and ash on the sand sheet. A disturbance of the eolian analog, not the analog itself.

name: Apollo geology training at Askja
coordinate_note: The opened Wikipedia page does not give a field-stop coordinate.
evidence_note: Historical astronaut geology training. Not a physical feature for similarity search.

name: Mauna Loa north flank
coordinate_note: The flank is context. The habitat point and the 6 km sample radius are child sites.
evidence_note: Young basaltic lava field. Distinct from the habitat simulation.

name: HI-SEAS habitat
coordinate_note: Wikipedia prints 19.602378 N, 155.487192 W and about 8200 ft (2500 m). Bleacher et al. 2017 say the station is at about 2400 m.
evidence_note: Isolation habitat on a former quarry on a spatter cone. Crew operations are not a ground feature.

name: Pahoehoe sample radius around HI-SEAS
coordinate_note: Center is the Wikipedia habitat point. Weert et al. 2021 sampled the top 10 cm of horizontal pahoehoe within a 6 km radius. The buffer is that radius, not a mapped flow outline.
evidence_note: Hydrous alteration in the top few centimeters of pahoehoe older than about 400 years.

name: North-flank lava tube segments
coordinate_note: Bleacher et al. 2017 do not print tube coordinates. They locate the work on the north flank near HI-SEAS. HI-SEAS habitat vicinity used solely as a provisional point; NOT a confirmed lava-tube entrance.
evidence_note: Two young tube segments mapped with GPR, magnetics, and lidar, and sampled for secondary salts.

name: Haughton impact structure
coordinate_note: Patterson and Ernst 2020: 75 deg 22 min 38 sec N, 89 deg 40 min 48 sec W. The Earth Impact Database page did not load, so it was not used for this point.
evidence_note: Carbonate and evaporite target. Apparent diameter about 23 km and rim diameter about 16 km in Osinski et al. 2005a. Age is contested.

name: Crater-fill impact melt breccia
coordinate_note: The opened hydrothermal abstract describes the unit and does not give a sample coordinate. Provisional location associated with published Haughton sampling; mapped unit membership requires verification.
evidence_note: Vugs and veins, with alteration intensity increasing toward the base. One of four hydrothermal settings.

name: Central uplift interior
coordinate_note: No sample coordinate in the opened abstract. Provisional location associated with published Haughton sampling; mapped unit membership requires verification.
evidence_note: Cementation and quartz mineralization in brecciated lithologies of the central uplift.

name: Outer margin of the central uplift
coordinate_note: No sample coordinate in the opened abstract. Provisional location associated with published Haughton sampling; mapped unit membership requires verification.
evidence_note: Intense calcite veining around the faulted outer margin of the central uplift.

name: Faulted crater-rim hydrothermal pipes
coordinate_note: No pipe coordinate in the opened abstract. Approximate northern crater-rim proxy, NOT a verified rim-fault or hydrothermal pipe.
evidence_note: Hydrothermal pipes or gossans and mineralization along rim faults.

name: Drill Hill
coordinate_note: Glass and Seitz 2021: 75 deg 25.25 min N, 89 deg 45.60 min W.
evidence_note: Fallback breccia with intermittent ice, used for planetary drill tests. Active layer about 50-70 cm in summer.

name: Flashline Mars Arctic Research Station
coordinate_note: Cockell et al. manuscript: 75 deg 25 min 52.39 sec N, 89 deg 49 min 28.05 sec W, 267.7 m, northwest rim.
evidence_note: Simulated lander and crew operations. Not a geological search seed.

name: Haughton-Mars Project Research Station
coordinate_note: Mars Institute page: 75 deg 26 min N, 89 deg 52 min W, northwestern rim. This is the project base camp, distinct from the FMARS coordinate.
evidence_note: Field base for science and exploration tests. Operations record only.

name: Haughton Formation paleolake sediments
coordinate_note: Mapped inside the central basin. No single outcrop coordinate was stored. Crater-centre proxy, NOT a verified Haughton Formation outcrop.
evidence_note: Post-impact lake sediments. A separate process from the hydrothermal system.

name: Haughton ice-wedge polygons
coordinate_note: Described as abundant patterned ground on carbonate-rich soils. Not one surveyed polygon. Crater-centre proxy, NOT a verified polygon field.
evidence_note: Ice-wedge polygons and a summer active layer about 50-70 cm thick.

name: Devon Island glacial trough valleys
coordinate_note: The project page illustrates Astronaut Canyon and does not print its coordinate.
evidence_note: Project interpretation that some Devon Island troughs resemble Martian canyon tributaries. Not used as a search seed.
